# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 77 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 77 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_077_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 7 — Why the Righteous Suffer

**1** A few days later I saw the Shepherd again in the same open plain where I had seen the other shepherds. "What do you want?" he asked me. **2** "Sir," I said, "I want you to order that punishing shepherd to leave my house — he's been tormenting me terribly." **3** "You have to go through this suffering," he said. "That's what the glorious angel ordered for you — he wants you to be tested and proven." **4** "But why?" I asked. "What wrong have I done that I've been handed over to this angel?" **5** "Let me explain," he said. "Your own sins are significant, but not serious enough to warrant this angel's attention. The problem is your household — they have committed serious wrongs and sins, and the glorious angel has grown deeply troubled over what they have done. That is why he ordered you to suffer for a time, hoping this will move them to turn back to God and be purified from every attachment to this world. **6** Once they truly repent and are cleansed, the angel of punishment will leave." **7** "But Lord," I said, "if they're the ones who have acted badly and upset the glorious angel, what did I do wrong?" He told me, "They simply cannot be brought to the point of change unless you — as the head of the family — go through suffering too. When you suffer, they suffer. When you're comfortable, they have no impetus to change." **8** "But Lord," I said, "look — they have genuinely turned back to God with all their heart!" **9** "I know they have," he replied. "But do you think that just because someone repents, their sins vanish immediately? That's not how it works. The person who repents must wrestle with their own soul, humble themselves deeply in every area of life, and pass through many difficult trials. If they endure those trials, then God — who made everything and filled it with power — will be moved with compassion and provide a remedy. **10** But that only happens when God sees that the heart of the penitent has become genuinely free of evil. So yes — it is actually for your good and your family's good that you're suffering now. Why go on at length? You must suffer as the Lord's angel commanded when he entrusted you to me. Give thanks to God for this: he thought enough of you to warn you ahead of time, so that knowing what was coming, you would have the strength to bear it."

---

*PNEUMA renders the suffering theology in accessible contemporary idiom while preserving the disciplinary logic of the original.*
